34	
35	    Parameters:
36	        > Parameters that control the model and reference model
37	
38	        model_init_kwargs (`str` or `dict[str, Any]`, *optional*):
39	            Keyword arguments for [`~transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained`], used when the `model`
40	            argument of the [`GRPOTrainer`] is provided as a string. The `revision` value is also used when loading
41	            processing classes.
42	        trust_remote_code (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
43	            Whether to allow loading models and tokenizers that ship custom Python code from the Hub. Forwarded to
44	            [`~transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained`] and [`~transformers.AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`].
45	            Also applied to reward-model and reward-tokenizer loads.
46	        router_aux_loss_coef (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.001`):
47	            Coefficient of the load-balancing auxiliary loss. Only has an effect when training a Mixture-of-Experts
48	            (MoE) model; for other models it does nothing. The auxiliary loss is added to the training loss with this
49	            weight. Set to `0.0` to disable it.
50	        disable_dropout (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
51	            Whether to disable dropout in the model. This is useful for training with a reference model, as it prevents
52	            the model from generating different logprobs for the same input.
53	        cast_lm_head_to_fp32 (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
54	            Whether to cast the language modeling head of the policy and reference models to float32. As recommended by
55	            the [ScaleRL](https://huggingface.co/papers/2510.13786) recipe. This flag is only supported when the model
56	            has untied word embedding and language modeling head layers i.e. `tie_word_embeddings` in the model config
57	            is False.
58	
59	        > Parameters that control the data preprocessing
60	
61	        remove_unused_columns (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
62	            Whether to only keep the column `"prompt"` in the dataset. If you use a custom reward function that
63	            requires any column other than `"prompts"` and `"completions"`, you should keep this to `False`.
64	        num_generations (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `8`):
65	            Number of generations per prompt to sample. The effective batch size (num_processes * per_device_batch_size
66	            * gradient_accumulation_steps) must be evenly divisible by this value.
67	        num_generations_eval (`int`, *optional*):
68	            Number of generations to sample during evaluation. This allows using fewer generations during evaluation to
69	            save computation. If `None`, uses the value of `num_generations`.
70	        max_completion_length (`int` or `None`, *optional*, defaults to `512`):
71	            Maximum length of the generated completion.
72	        ds3_gather_for_generation (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):

74	            improving generation speed. However, disabling this option allows training models that exceed the VRAM
75	            capacity of a single GPU, albeit at the cost of slower generation. Disabling this option is not compatible
76	            with vLLM generation.
77	        shuffle_dataset (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
78	            Whether to shuffle the training dataset.
79	        pad_to_multiple_of (`int`, *optional*):
80	            If set, the prompts ids and completions ids will be padded to a multiple of this value.
81	
82	        > Parameters that control generation
83	
84	        generation_batch_size (`int`, *optional*):
85	            Batch size to use for generation. If `None`, it defaults to the effective training batch size:
86	            `per_device_train_batch_size * num_processes * steps_per_generation`. In other words, there is one
87	            generation batch processed per optimization step. Mutually exclusive with `steps_per_generation`.
88	        steps_per_generation (`int`, *optional*):
89	            Number of steps per generation. If `None`, it defaults to `gradient_accumulation_steps`. Mutually exclusive
90	            with `generation_batch_size`.
91	        temperature (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
92	            Temperature for sampling. The higher the temperature, the more random the completions.
93	        top_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
94	            Float that controls the cumulative probability of the top tokens to consider. Must be in (0, 1]. Set to
95	            `1.0` to consider all tokens.
96	        top_k (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):

99	        min_p (`float`, *optional*):
100	            Minimum token probability, which will be scaled by the probability of the most likely token. It must be a
101	            value between `0.0` and `1.0`. Typical values are in the `0.01-0.2` range.
102	        generation_kwargs (`dict[str, Any]`, *optional*):
103	            Additional keyword arguments to pass to [`~transformers.GenerationConfig`] (if using transformers) or
104	            `SamplingParams` (if using vLLM) when sampling completions. This can be used to further customize the
105	            generation behavior, such as setting `suppress_tokens`, `num_beams`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict
106	            with the other generation parameters (like `min_p`, `top_p`, etc.), they will override them.
107	        chat_template_kwargs (`dict[str, Any]`, *optional*):
108	            Additional keyword arguments to pass to the `apply_chat_template` function when generating completions.
109	        repetition_penalty (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
110	            Float that penalizes new tokens based on whether they appear in the prompt and the generated text so far.
111	            Values > `1.0` encourage the model to use new tokens, while values < `1.0` encourage the model to repeat
112	            tokens.
113	        cache_implementation (`str`, *optional*):
114	            Implementation of the cache method for faster generation when `use_vllm` is set to `False`.
115

121	        vllm_mode (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"colocate"`):

130	            Model implementation to use for vLLM. Must be one of `"transformers"` or `"vllm"`. `"transformers"`: Use
131	            the `transformers` backend for model implementation. `"vllm"`: Use the `vllm` library for model
132	            implementation.
133	        vllm_enable_sleep_mode (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
134	            Enable vLLM sleep mode to offload weights/cache during the optimizer step. Keeps GPU memory usage low, but
135	            waking the engine adds host–device transfer latency.
136	        vllm_structured_outputs_regex (`str`, *optional*):
137	            Regex for vLLM structured outputs. If `None` (default), structured outputs is disabled.
138	
139	        > Parameters that control the vLLM server (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"server"`)
140	
141	        vllm_server_base_url (`str`, *optional*):
142	            Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., `"http://localhost:8000"`). If provided, `vllm_server_host` and
143	            `vllm_server_port` are ignored.
144	        vllm_server_host (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"0.0.0.0"`):
145	            Host of the vLLM server to connect to. Ignored if `vllm_server_base_url` is provided.
146	        vllm_server_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `8000`):
147	            Port of the vLLM server to connect to. Ignored if `vllm_server_base_url` is provided.
148	        vllm_server_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `240.0`):
149	            Total timeout duration in seconds to wait for the vLLM server to be up. If the server is not up after the
150	            timeout, a `ConnectionError` is raised.
151	        vllm_group_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `51216`):

153	            is occupied, there is no need to change it.
154	
155	        > Parameters that control colocated vLLM execution (only used when `vllm_mode` is `"colocate"`)
156	
157	        vllm_gpu_memory_utilization (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.3`):
158	            Control the GPU memory utilization for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to
159	            `"colocate"`. If you are using `vllm_mode="server"`, this parameter must be passed separately when
160	            launching the vLLM server via the `--vllm_gpu_memory_utilization` flag.
161	        vllm_max_model_length (`int`, *optional*):
162	            Context window for vLLM. Set it to at least the maximum prompt length in the dataset plus

165	            Control the tensor parallel size for vLLM. This setting only applies when `vllm_mode` is set to

168	
169	        > Parameters that control the training
170	
171	        beta (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
172	            KL coefficient. If `0.0` (default), the reference model is not loaded, reducing memory usage and improving
173	            training speed. [DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement
174	            learning](https://huggingface.co/papers/2501.12948) use a value of `0.001`.
175	        num_iterations (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
176	            Number of iterations per batch (denoted as μ in the algorithm).
177	        epsilon (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.2`):
178	            Epsilon value for clipping.
179	        delta (`float`, *optional*):
180	            Enables the upper clipping bound in two-sided GRPO loss when set to a float. If `None` (default), standard
181	            GRPO clipping is used. Recommended to be greater than `1 + ε` when enabled. This method is introduced in
182	            the [INTELLECT-2 tech report](https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.07291).
183	        epsilon_high (`float`, *optional*):
184	            Upper-bound epsilon value for clipping. If not specified, it defaults to the same value as the lower-bound
185	            specified in argument `epsilon`. Paper [DAPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) recommends `0.28`.
186	            When used with `loss_type='cispo'`, this corresponds to the ε_max param specified in the [ScaleRL
187	            paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2510.13786) and the recommended value is `5.0`.
188	        sapo_temperature_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.05`):
189	            Temperature for tokens with non-positive advantage scores used in the `sapo` loss function. This parameter
190	            is introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347).
191	        sapo_temperature_pos (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
192	            Temperature for tokens with positive advantage scores used in the `sapo` loss function. This parameter is
193	            introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347).
194	        vespo_k_pos (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
195	            k parameter for positive advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively
196	            we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).
197	        vespo_lambda_pos (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `3.0`):
198	            lambda parameter for positive advantages, it is the decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls how
199	            aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio > 1).
200	        vespo_k_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `3.0`):
201	            k parameter for negative advantages, it is the power exponent in the VESPO loss. Controls how aggressively
202	            we down-weight samples with low importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio < 1).
203	        vespo_lambda_neg (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
204	            lambda parameter for negative advantages, it is the exponential decay factor in the VESPO loss. Controls
205	            how aggressively we down-weight samples with high importance weights (when the importance sampling ratio >
206	            1).
207	        importance_sampling_level (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"token"`):
208	            Controls whether importance sampling ratios are computed at the `"token"` or `"sequence"` level. `"token"`
209	            keeps the raw per-token log-probability ratios (one weight per token). `"sequence"` averages the
210	            log-probability ratios across valid tokens to produce a single ratio per sequence. The [GSPO
211	            paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2507.18071) shows that sequence-level sampling often yields more
212	            stable training and better alignment with sequence-level rewards.
213	        reward_weights (`list[float]`, *optional*):
214	            Weights for each reward function. Must match the number of reward functions. If `None`, all rewards are
215	            weighted equally with weight `1.0`.
216	        multi_objective_aggregation (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"sum_then_normalize"`):
217	            Method to aggregate multiple reward functions. Supported values are:
218	
219	            - `"sum_then_normalize"` (default): First sums the weighted rewards from each reward function, then applies
220	              reward scaling/normalization as specified by `scale_rewards` (see `scale_rewards` for details).
221	            - `"normalize_then_sum"`: First normalizes/scales each reward function across generations (within each
222	              group), then sums the normalized rewards using the specified weights. The aggregated reward is then
223	              normalized at the batch level when forming advantages. This is the suggested approach from the paper
224	              [GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL
225	              Optimization](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.05242).
226	        scale_rewards (`str` or `bool`, *optional*, defaults to `"group"`):
227	            Specifies the scaling strategy for rewards. Supported values are:
228	
229	            - `True` or `"group"` (default): rewards are scaled by the standard deviation within each group, ensuring
230	              unit variance within a group.
231	            - `"batch"`: rewards are scaled by the standard deviation across the entire batch, as recommended in the
232	              [PPO Lite paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2508.08221).
233	            - `False` or `"none"`: no scaling is applied. The [Dr. GRPO
234	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.20783) recommends not scaling rewards, as scaling by the
235	              standard deviation introduces a question-level difficulty bias.
236	        loss_type (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"dapo"`):
237	            Specifies the loss formulation to use. Supported values are:
238	
239	            - `"grpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing over sequence length. Not recommended due to
240	              length bias—this approach tends to prefer shorter completions with positive advantages and longer ones
241	              with negative advantages.
242	            - `"dr_grpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with a global constant. This method was
243	              introduced in the [Dr. GRPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.20783) to eliminate length bias.
244	              The value of the constant corresponds to `max_completion_length`.
245	            - `"dapo"` (default): Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the
246	              global accumulated batch. This method was introduced in the [DAPO
247	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) to eliminate length bias.
248	            - `"bnpo"`: Aggregates token-level losses by normalizing with the number of active token in the local
249	              batch. Note that normalization is performed over the local batch only, so results may slightly vary
250	              depending on the local batch size, despite a constant effective batch size. When using
251	              `per_device_train_batch_size==1`, the loss is equivalent to the GRPO loss.
252	            - `"cispo"`: Clips the importance sampling weights instead of the advantage scaled importance weights. The
253	              clipped weights are then multiplied with the advantages and policy model's log probs. Individual token
254	              losses are aggregated by normalizing with the number of active tokens in the global accumulated batch.
255	              This method was introduced in the [MiniMax-M1 paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.13585).
256	            - `"sapo"`: Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization loss, as introduced in the [Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization
257	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2511.20347). Replaces hard clipping with a smooth,
258	              temperature-controlled gate that adaptively attenuates off-policy updates while preserving useful
259	              learning signals.
260	            - `"luspo"`: Length-Unbiased Sequence Policy Optimization loss. A sequence-level loss that scales each
261	              sequence's loss by its length. This is a modification of GSPO and requires
262	              `importance_sampling_level="sequence"`. Introduced in the [LUSPO
263	              paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.05261).
264	            - `"vespo"`: Variational Sequence-Level Soft Policy Optimization. Replaces hard clipping with a smooth,
265	              asymmetric Gamma weighting function applied directly to sequence-level importance weights. Introduced in
266	              the [VESPO paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.10693).
267	        mask_truncated_completions (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
268	            When enabled, truncated completions are excluded from the loss calculation, preventing them from being
269	            incorrectly penalized and introducing noise during training. According to the
270	            [DAPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2503.14476) paper, this is a good practice for training stability.
271	        sync_ref_model (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
272	            Whether to synchronize the reference model with the active model every `ref_model_sync_steps` steps, using
273	            the `ref_model_mixup_alpha` parameter. This synchronization originates from the
274	            [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper.
275	        ref_model_mixup_alpha (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.6`):
276	            α parameter from the [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper, which controls the mix
277	            between the current policy and the previous reference policy during updates. The reference policy is
278	            updated according to the equation: `π_ref = α * π_θ + (1 - α) * π_ref_prev`. To use this parameter, you
279	            must set `sync_ref_model=True`.
280	        ref_model_sync_steps (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `512`):
281	            τ parameter from the [TR-DPO](https://huggingface.co/papers/2404.09656) paper, which determines how
282	            frequently the current policy is synchronized with the reference policy. To use this parameter, you must
283	            set `sync_ref_model=True`.
284	        top_entropy_quantile (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
285	            ρ parameter from [Beyond the 80/20 Rule](https://huggingface.co/papers/2506.01939). Keeps in the policy
286	            loss term only the top-ρ quantile of tokens by entropy of the probability distribution at each sequence
287	            position, improving results. Range: `[0.0-1.0]`. A value of `0.0` masks all but the highest entropy token;
288	            `1.0` keeps all tokens. The paper recommends a value of `0.2`. If used with
289	            `mask_truncated_completions=True`, only tokens from non-truncated completions are considered.
290	        entropy_coef (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
291	            Coefficient of the entropy regularization term in the loss. A positive value adds an entropy bonus that
292	            encourages exploration by keeping the policy from collapsing to near-deterministic outputs. The bonus is
293	            always the mean per-token entropy regardless of `loss_type`; it is not rescaled to match a loss type's
294	            policy normalization, so `entropy_coef` has the same meaning for every loss type. When
295	            `use_adaptive_entropy=True`, this serves as the initial coefficient and is updated each optimizer step. Has
296	            no effect when set to `0.0` (default).
297	        use_adaptive_entropy (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `False`):
298	            Whether to use adaptive entropy control, introduced in
299	            [Skywork-OR1](https://huggingface.co/papers/2505.22312). When enabled, the entropy coefficient
300	            `entropy_coef` is updated each optimizer step: incremented by `entropy_coef_delta` when the current entropy
301	            is below `entropy_target`, and decremented otherwise. The coefficient is only applied when entropy is at or
302	            below `entropy_target`.
303	        entropy_coef_min (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
304	            Lower bound for the entropy coefficient when using adaptive entropy control.
305	        entropy_coef_max (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
306	            Upper bound for the entropy coefficient when using adaptive entropy control.
307	        entropy_coef_delta (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.005`):
308	            Step size for adjusting the entropy coefficient at each optimizer step during adaptive entropy control.
309	        entropy_target (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.2`):
310	            Target mean per-token entropy (in nats) used by adaptive entropy control. The coefficient is only applied
311	            when the current entropy falls at or below this value. Measured over the same token set as the policy loss:
312	            all completion tokens by default, or only the high-entropy subset when `top_entropy_quantile < 1.0`.
313	            Typical language models have per-token entropies in the range 2–10 nats, so the default of `0.2` almost
314	            never triggers regularization (only on near-complete entropy collapse); set it close to the entropy you
315	            observe early in training (logged as the `entropy` metric) so the bonus engages before the policy collapses
316	            (and account for the token subset when using `top_entropy_quantile`).
317	        max_tool_calling_iterations (`int`, *optional*):

325	            and constrained.
326	        vllm_importance_sampling_mode (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"sequence_mask"`):
327	            Specifies how Importance Sampling is performed when `vllm_importance_sampling_correction=True`. Possible
328	            values are:
329	
330	                - `"token_truncate"`: Token-level truncated IS (default). Per-token ratios are clipped to
331	                [C_min, C_max].
332	                - `"token_mask"`: Token-level masked IS. Per-token ratios outside [C_min, C_max] are set to zero.
333	                - `"sequence_truncate"`: Sequence-level truncated IS. A single sequence ratio is clipped to
334	                [C_min, C_max] and applied to all tokens in the sequence.
335	                - `"sequence_mask"`: Sequence-level masked IS. Sequences with ratios outside [C_min, C_max] are masked
336	                out.
337	        vllm_importance_sampling_clip_max (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `3.0`):
338	            Importance sampling upper bound C_max used by `vllm_importance_sampling_mode`. For `*_truncate` modes,
